## Description of Changes

Adds a FORMAT variable for a more strict RFC3339 where the RFC called for a space for readability and is used by FORMAT_RFC3339, FORMAT_RFC3339_STRICT uses the T separator to adhere with ISO8601 spec.

[RFC Link](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3339#section-5.6)
```
      NOTE: ISO 8601 defines date and time separated by "T".
      Applications using this syntax may choose, for the sake of
      readability, to specify a full-date and full-time separated by
      (say) a space character.
```

Closes #1138

import arrow
from datetime import datetime

dt = datetime(2023, 10, 27, 12, 30, 45)
arrow_dt = arrow.get(dt)

# Note: we need a timezone for ZZ to work properly, or it might use UTC
# Let's use UTC
arrow_dt = arrow_dt.to('UTC')

fmt_rfc3339 = arrow_dt.format(arrow.FORMAT_RFC3339)
fmt_rfc3339_strict = arrow_dt.format(arrow.FORMAT_RFC3339_STRICT)

print(f"RFC3339: {fmt_rfc3339}")
print(f"RFC3339_STRICT: {fmt_rfc3339_strict}")

assert " " in fmt_rfc3339
assert "T" in fmt_rfc3339_strict
assert fmt_rfc3339.replace(" ", "T") == fmt_rfc3339_strict

print("Tests passed!")
